## Hi, I'm Julius 👋

I'm a PhD candidate working on how we can design and operate the energy systems of a climate-neutral future more efficiently. My research sits at the intersection of **system simulation** and **scientific machine learning**: I combine physics-based models with machine learning, for example as fast surrogate models, to make optimization of technical assets practical at scale. Part of this work happens in the European research project [OpenSCALING](https://itea4.org/project/openscaling.html).

I came to this field through energy engineering. I studied **Energy Systems** at the Hamburg University of Technology (TUHH) and spent an exchange year at **UC Berkeley**. Along the way, I built machine-learning surrogates for complex system models at XRG Simulation in the research project [PHyMoS](https://phymos.de/), developed a charging-depot controller for automated vehicle fleets at **Berkeley Lab** in the project [GEMINI-XFC](https://www.energy.gov/eere/vehicles/articles/grid-enhanced-mobility-integrated-network-infrastructures-extreme-fast-0), worked on thermal energy storage at **Siemens Gamesa**, and taught first-year students as a tutor. The full story is in my [CV](cv.qmd).

### What this blog is about

Mostly the **energy transition**: how the energy system of the future could work, and what each of us can do about it. Besides that, I'll write about my **research** and about something I've been tinkering with a lot lately, **AI agents**. Some posts are in English, some in [German](blog_ger.qmd).

:::

## Publications

I publish on different techniques that I hope will improve and enable more widespread use of simulation and optimization in energy systems. You can find the list on the [publications page](publications.qmd).

## Get in touch

I'm always happy to talk about energy systems, simulation and machine learning, whether you're a researcher, someone from industry or just curious. Send me an email or connect with me on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/julius-aka/).
